deploy.why: Antigravity reads global rules from ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md and caps EACH rules file at 12000 characters (antigravity.google/docs/rules-workflows). AGENTS.md is 21851 characters, so a full copy cannot be delivered here; this target receives the compact doctrine payload instead. The file is shared with Gemini CLI, so injection is append-and-replace-in-place, never an overwrite.

Codex reads ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (or AGENTS.override.md in preference) and stops adding files once the global+project chain reaches project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md). A 21851-character global copy would crowd out the repo's own AGENTS.md, which is the more specific file, so this target receives the compact payload.

bind_comment: The third mode beside `deploy` and `presence` (HARNESS-045, #561): what a
persona's own claim — 'your phase's skills are enforced by hook, not left to
memory' — actually compiles to. Presence asks; bind enforces.
EVERY EVENT NAME BELOW WAS MEASURED against the installed harness, not taken
from ADR-027, whose render kinds were already stale in 2 of 5 (#563).
TWO FAMILIES, NOT FOUR CASES:
command-hook  a process receives the event as JSON on stdin and answers
with an exit code. claude and agy both use this, and agy
uses claude's exact `{hooks:[{type:command,...}]}` shape.
ts-extension  an in-process TypeScript handler. pi's `tool_call` returns
{block:true,reason}; opencode sets output.status='deny'.
The wrapper is generated here, so it emits ONE canonical
payload rather than each harness's own — which deletes two
parsers instead of adding them.
`agy` IS NOT PRESENCE-ONLY. #561 defers it on the assumption that it has no
gate. Measured: ~/.gemini/settings.json declares BeforeAgent, AfterAgent,
BeforeTool, AfterTool. It is the CHEAPEST harness to add after claude, not a
deferred one. Its groups carry no `matcher` key, hence `matcher: false` —
declared per harness rather than assumed from a family resemblance.
`opencode`'s gate is `permission.ask`, NOT `tool.execute.before`. The latter
is typed (input, output:{args}) => Promise<void>: it mutates arguments and
returns nothing, so it cannot deny. #561 and ADR-027 name the wrong event.
COEXISTENCE IS THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT, not an edge case. Orca owns 10 of
claude's 12 hook events on the measured machine — including PreToolUse — and
all four of agy's, and writes real .ts files into pi's extensions dir. So
emission is find-by-marker and additive: ours is replaced in place, absent
ours is appended as a NEW group, and a foreign entry is never reordered,
rewritten or removed. That also retires a positional bug: the shell path
writes `.hooks.<event>[0].hooks[0].command`, which silently overwrites
whatever a third party put at index 0.
`emit: false` means DECLARED BUT NOT YET EMITTED — the gap is recorded here
so it is visible rather than remembered. See specs/HARNESS-045-hook-emission.
